ws1.does_it_look_for_existing_install: Yes, but only for the NEW scheme: it reads HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Sutram, and if registered AND InstallLocation is a DIFFERENT dir than the requested InstallDir AND that dir has a valid Sutram marker (.sutram-install containing exactly 'Sutram Windows installation'), it throws 'Sutram is already installed at: {registeredDir}. Uninstall that copy first, or choose the same installation folder.' If the registered dir is the SAME as InstallDir, it proceeds (upgrade in place). If the registry key does not exist or the registered dir has no marker, it does not throw. It does NOT look for the OLD installation (AppData\Local\Sutram, from the retired NSIS installer: HKLM, not HKCU; a different folder, not under LOCALAPPDATA\Programs; no .sutram-install marker) — so the old install is invisible to it. That is why two installations coexist.
ws1.hang_mechanism: No Read-Host, no Pause, no -Wait, and no unbounded loop in install-core.ps1, the wizard, or the build scripts (verified by grep). The only unbounded wait is the wizard's WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE) (sutram_wizard.asm:1145-1146): after CreateProcessW launches PowerShell with install-core.ps1, the wizard waits unbounded (no timeout, no cancel) for PowerShell to exit. If PowerShell is slow or stuck, the wizard sits at 60% forever and PowerShell remains open — exactly what was reported. The log ends at 'Copying Sutram files.' (step 7 of 12, before the post-install self-test, PATH, shortcuts, associations, registry, state, and 'Installation complete'), so the stall is in (or just after) the copy — most likely in Copy-Item itself (no timeout, no progress logging; the payload is 10-20 MB in hundreds of files and could be slow on a slow disk or with antivirus scanning, or a single file could be locked/stuck). Whether it was slow (and interrupted) or stuck cannot be determined from the log alone (the log does not say how long they waited, and there is no progress line during the copy), and I cannot run Windows here to reproduce it. What the code establishes is: (a) there is no prompt, so it is not waiting for input; (b) the wizard waits unbounded, so any stall in PowerShell looks like a hang; (c) the stall is in/just after the copy, before the self-test.
ws1.last_thing_before_exit: In install-core.ps1: log 'Installation complete: <InstallDir>', copy the log to InstallDir\install.log, append InstallLogSHA256 to install-state.ini, remove the stage dir (finally block), then exit 0. In the wizard: after PowerShell exits 0, remove the temp staging dir (%TEMP%\STM*.tmp), report success, exit. The tester's log ends at 'Copying Sutram files.' (step 7), before the post-install self-test (step 8), PATH (step 9), shortcuts (step 10), associations/registry (step 11), state (step 12), and 'Installation complete' — so it stopped after the copy started but before any of those.
ws1.steps_summary: build-windows-setup.ps1 is the BUILD (runs preflight, build-windows-native, gui/build-gui, native-installer/build-installer; builds Sutram-Setup.exe; installs nothing — it says so). build-common.ps1 is build helpers only (Invoke-BoundedProcess with a 20 s timeout, Assert-Pe64, icon resources). sutram-installer.nsi is RETIRED (HKLM/admin, needs UAC, cannot be shipped; superseded by windows/native-installer/; kept only as history — and it is the old installer that wrote the old installation). build-installer.ps1 builds Sutram-Setup.exe (stages payload, writes SHA-256 manifest, zips payload.zip, embeds SHA-256 hashes of payload/install-core/uninstall-core/LICENSE into the wizard, assembles sutram_wizard.asm with nasm+ld, runs --self-test, writes Sutram-Setup.sha256). The install-time engine is the wizard (Sutram-Setup.exe, sutram_wizard.asm) + install-core.ps1 (embedded via incbin, extracted to temp, run via powershell.exe -NoProfile -File). install-core.ps1 (12 steps, in order): log header + preconditions (64-bit OS/process, payload/setup-exe exist); InstallDir validation (per-user only, under LOCALAPPDATA\Programs, length <=220, no UNC, no shell metachars, no ';' if AddPath, not a drive root, not WINDIR/SystemRoot/ProgramFiles/USERPROFILE); existing-install check (HKCU uninstall + marker, NEW scheme only); folder/marker/ownership checks (non-empty non-Sutram folder refused; conflicting Sutram.Source registration refused; incomplete ownership metadata refused; modified uninstaller refused); stage + Verify-Payload (SHA-256 manifest, every file must exist and match, no unmanifested files) + pre-install self-tests (--version/--help, bounded 8 s each, must exit 0 + non-empty stdout) + VerifyOnly (exits 0, no install); upgrade safety (refuses to overwrite user-modified files); remove old payload (preserving user-modified files) + Copy-Item (logs 'Copying Sutram files.') + marker; post-install self-test (--version, bounded 8 s); PATH (user only, see ws2); shortcuts (Start Menu + Desktop, preserving pre-existing user shortcuts); file associations + uninstall registry (DisplayVersion hardcoded 0.1.0 — see follow-ups); state file + 'Installation complete' + log copy + exit 0. Every throw goes to catch (logs ERROR, exits 1).
ws1.which_path_entry: User only. It writes to HKCU\Environment (the current-user PATH), via Set-UserPathEntry in install-core.ps1, and only the bin dir ($InstallDir\bin, i.e. AppData\Local\Programs\Sutram\bin), and only if -AddPath was passed (the wizard passes it from the GUI checkbox). It never writes to the machine PATH (HKLM), and it never reads, removes, or checks the machine PATH. The retired NSIS installer wrote to the machine PATH (EnVar::SetHKLM, EnVar::AddValue 'Path' '$INSTDIR\bin'), which is why the old installation has a machine PATH entry.

ws2.order: 1. C:\Users\dmech\AppData\Local\Sutram\bin — older, machine PATH, WINS (from the retired NSIS installer; the new installer does not see it, does not remove it, and cannot remove it without admin rights). 2. C:\Users\dmech\AppData\Local\Programs\Sutram\bin — newer, user PATH, LOSES (from the new installer; it is added correctly, but it is searched after the machine PATH). On Windows, when a command is resolved, the system (machine) PATH is searched before the user PATH (a process's PATH is constructed as machine PATH + user PATH, in that order). So the older machine entry is searched before the newer user entry, the older version wins, and a student typing 'sutram' in a fresh cmd.exe gets Sutram 1.4.0 (the old one), not v303/v305 (the new one). Nothing tells the student this. The installer writes only to user PATH, so it cannot fix the old machine entry (it does not even look at it, and removing a machine PATH entry would require administrator rights, which a per-user installer (no UAC prompt, by design) does not have). The fix (for Claude/owner) is for the installer to detect the old machine PATH entry (and the old installation) and warn the user — or refuse to proceed until the old copy is uninstalled — rather than silently installing a second copy that loses on PATH. (Removing the machine entry itself needs admin/UAC, so the installer should tell the user to uninstall the old copy first, or offer to do it with elevation.) The existing-install check should also be extended to look for the old installation (old path, old HKLM registry, old machine PATH entry), not just for the new-scheme HKCU registration — otherwise it will keep missing the old copy, as it did here.

ws3.test_description_file: r132_clean_shell_test.md (delivered with this round, for Claude to build). In short: a clean-shell check that the installer completes AND that 'sutram --version' in a fresh shell resolves to the installed version. It must: start from a machine with an OLD installation present (to catch the PATH conflict, not just a clean machine); run the installer with a timeout (e.g. 120 s, fail if it does not exit); assert it exits 0 and the log reaches 'Installation complete' (not just 'Copying Sutram files.'); assert no powershell.exe or Sutram-Setup.exe lingers after it exits; then open a FRESH cmd.exe (a new process, so it picks up the new PATH) and run bare 'sutram --version' and 'where sutram', and assert the version matches the installed version (v305) and the resolved path is the new install dir (AppData\Local\Programs\Sutram\bin\sutram.exe), not the old one (AppData\Local\Sutram\bin). It should also assert the uninstall entry's DisplayVersion is the installed version (not the hardcoded 0.1.0 found in WS1). See the file for the full steps, setup, assertions, and timeouts. It must NOT mark installation successful just because the compiler file was copied (copying sutram.exe is step 7 of 12, not the end); it must NOT reuse a shell that was open before the install (that shell would have the old PATH); and it must NOT run on a clean machine only (a clean machine has no old installation, so defect 2 would not appear).
